components.html:
Casting a fireball

Show one open palm toward the camera and keep it visible for a moment. A fireball launches from your palm toward you. Close your hand briefly, then reopen it to cast again. Both hands can cast independently.

Keep your fingers visible and use even lighting. A brief cooldown separates casts. With reduced motion enabled, the fireball becomes a soft, stationary glow without flying embers.

narrative.overview:
An Experience surface: the live webcam is the work. The portfolio’s deep purple ground, Neoris text, Seasons italics, pale lavender ink, and thin rules remain the visual authority. The title is compact so the camera occupies most of the first view. This document records the implemented Domain Expansion surface and its Fireball mode, not new rules for the whole portfolio.

Before camera permission, an authored two-hand diagram explains the Domain frame; Fireball replaces it with a single open palm, a warm glow, and a directional arrow. A two-mode selector above the stage changes the guidance and effect. Start camera is the primary action. During startup, Stop remains outside the loading overlay. During play, controls remain below the camera rather than obscuring the effect. The same controls and reading order persist on phones; the Domain pixel slider becomes a second row and hides in Fireball mode.
keyCharacteristics: A large, square-cornered camera stage with a restrained editorial frame.
Neoris interface text paired with Seasons italic emphasis.
Pale lavender controls and an anime-inspired violet Domain boundary, with gold-orange selection and fire in Fireball mode.
Explicit camera states and readable text over changing footage.

rules.name: The Live Text Rule
rules.body: Live camera labels and status text keep their individual dark backings as well as the stage-edge gradients. Footage must not become their only background.

dos: **Do** preserve Neoris and Seasons, the purple ground, pale lavender ink, and thin rules.
**Do** keep Start camera prominent and Stop reachable during loading.
**Do** keep live labels on their dark backings and retain visible keyboard focus.
**Do** preserve the mobile control order and native labeled slider in Domain mode; hide the slider in Fireball mode.
**Do** retain the Domain boundary and fingertip points under reduced motion, and use a stationary fading glow for Fireball.
**Do** use the local gold-orange accent, one-palm guide, and mode-specific help for Fireball while preserving the shared purple frame.
**Do** preserve native radio selection and visible focus when switching effects.
donts: **Don't** move controls over the live effect.
**Don't** apply Domain pixelation outside the fingertip-defined window; finger outlines and the boundary glow may extend outside it.
**Don't** restore the decorative stage label or lose sentence spacing on mobile.
**Don't** treat synthetic captures as evidence of physical hand-tracking accuracy.
